title: UAE cybersecurity chief says Iranian actors used wipers against UAE systems
summary: At the World Police Summit in Dubai, Dr Mohamed Al Kuwaiti, described by The National as the UAE's cybersecurity chief, said Iran used destructive wipers that erase data rather than lock systems for ransom. Wiper malware was used in attempts targeting electricity, water, desalination, education and healthcare systems, he said, and AI agents made attack origins hard to trace.
plain: The UAE's cybersecurity chief said Iran used data-destroying malware in attempts targeting UAE electricity, water, desalination, education and healthcare systems, according to The National.
exec: A government says wiper malware, not just ransomware, was used against national infrastructure; plan for destructive attacks.
action: Keep offline, tested backups and rehearse restoring critical systems, since wipers erase data rather than demand ransom.

validation.note: One publisher read; the claim is the official's own speech. No incident dates or forensic detail given.

review.note: The National says wipers were used in attempts targeting sectors, not that they hit them; summary and plain softened; org no longer names a council the article does not mention
